messages:
Maria: Hey team, saw a weird terraform plan in staging after I changed the module to conditionally create TG attachments via count. Plan wants to destroy + recreate 18 attachments even though I only toggled a feature flag. Any quick ideas?
Jon: can you paste the small resource snippet? count-related diffs usually come from computed values.
Maria: here ya go:
```hcl
resource "aws_lb_target_group_attachment" "tg" {
  count = var.enable_service && length(var.targets) > 0 ? length(var.targets) : 0
  target_group_arn = aws_lb_target_group.main.arn
  target_id        = var.targets[count.index]
  port             = var.port
}
```
Maria: note var.targets is computed from a module output that can change during apply.
Jon: yup, count + computed list is brittle. terraform evaluates count during plan but if the list is unknown it can flip. for_each with a stable key is safer.
Sam: also check state vs imported attachments. If some attachments were imported earlier with different indexing, plan will try to reconcile by recreating. run `terraform state list | grep aws_lb_target_group_attachment` and see indexes.
Leah: quick workaround: create a local stable map for for_each, e.g. locals.targets_map = { for idx,t in toset(var.targets) : t => idx } then for_each = local.targets_map. Avoids positional reindexing.
Maria: oof we also hit a lock from CI when I was testing. Infra-bot said it acquired a lock.
Infra-bot: Lock acquired on workspace"redwood-staging" by CI-runner-57 for run 2983.
Jon: CI lock could block apply but not plan, right?
Sam: plan can run but apply will be blocked. However if CI did an import/partial apply earlier that changed state, that explains the diff.
Maria: I checked state list — indexes 0..17 exist but target ids mismatch because module output ordering changed.
Leah: two long-term fixes: 1) switch to for_each with stable keys 2) avoid deriving targets order from external dynamic sources, or sort them in module.
Jon: if you want quick fix: import the specific attachments into the new indexing or taint the problematic ones and let apply recreate them. Example: `terraform import aws_lb_target_group_attachment.tg["i-abc123"] <tg-arn>/<instance-id>` (depending on how you map keys).
Maria: I'm going to convert to for_each + stable set and run plan. Will ping if it still wants to recreate.
Infra-bot: Lock released on workspace"redwood-staging" by CI-runner-57.
Maria: OK switched to for_each using a sorted(var.targets) -> map with instance id keys, ran `terraform plan` and the huge recreate is gone. Only a harmless metadata change.
Sam: nice. If you want, we can add a small eval in the module tests to ensure target ordering is stable.
Maria: will do. Thanks all :thumbsup:
Leah: nice fix — can you open a tiny PR describing the change so we can roll it to prod later?
Maria: will open PR now, link when ready.
Jon: reassigning to infra-owner for review once PR is up.
Maria: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/472 — contains the for_each refactor + unit test.
Sam: reviewing shortly.
Maria: closing the thread — plan looks clean in staging and I imported one edge-case attachment that was previously unmanaged.
Leah: thanks for the writeup.
Maria: np, cheers!
